place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 正殿前 · 大比擂台
place.en: Chending Temple · Before the main hall · the contest platform

setup.zh: 外门大比。名册上三百多个名字，大半弃了权，剩下六十几个人上台；人人都押马小宝——他练气五层了，马家为了这一枚筑基丹，把蒙山上的树卖了三成。
setup.en: The outer court contest. Three hundred-odd names are on the register, most have withdrawn, sixty-some will fight — and everyone is betting on Ma Xiaobao — he is at layer five now, and the Ma family sold three-tenths of the trees on Mount Meng for this one Foundation pill.

recap.zh: 腊月初八，外门大比开场：所有人都押马小宝。抽签，你对孙二狗。
recap.en: The eighth of the twelfth month, the contest opens: everyone backs Ma Xiaobao. The lots: you against Sun Ergou.

zh: 头名，筑基丹一枚。整个沉鼎观，只一枚。
en: The eighth of the twelfth month: the outer court contest.
First place: one Foundation pill. The only one the temple has.
Everyone is betting on Ma Xiaobao.

story.zh:
大比的台子搭在外门的演武场上，五块青石板拼成一个圆，缝里都长出了草，名字倒大，叫五行台——台上并没有五行，只有五块石头。外门大比，向来是一日打完的。名册上三百多个名字，大半都画了圈，末了剩下六十几个人，捉对厮杀，输一场便下去。一场只给半炷香，香到了分不出胜负，执事便看谁站得离台心近，谁近谁赢。

抽签的时候，周衡坐在竹筒旁边，一个名字一个名字往大比的名录上誊。那名录是一本老账簿，蓝布面，边角都给翻烂了，前头几十页记的是历年的大比，一年一页，一页上头一行，写的是那一年的头名。小满排到周衡跟前，瞧见那名录正翻在前头，墨色从新到旧，旧到后来，黄得像秋天的树叶。有一页上，头名那一行的名字给人拿笔划了一道，划得很直，划过去的墨比字的墨还新些，底下的名字给水渍洇开了，看不清写的是什么。

小满问道：「周师兄，这一个怎么划了？」周衡头也不抬：「划了的，是不在观里了的。」小满道：「死了？」周衡道：「不在观里了。账上只记在不在，不记为什么。为什么，不归我管。」说罢冲他一伸手，「签。」小满把手伸进竹筒里。执事念道：「沈小满——对，孙二狗。」台下有人笑出了声。
story.en:
The contest stage stood on the outer court's training ground, five bluestone slabs laid in a circle, grass grown in the seams, and a big name for it: the Five Elements Platform — with no five elements on it, only five stones. The outer court contest was always fought in one day. Three hundred-odd names on the register; most had circled their names, leaving sixty-some to be paired off, one loss and out. Each bout got half a stick of incense; if nobody won by the time it burned out, the steward looked at who stood nearer the centre, and nearer won.

While lots were drawn, Zhou Heng sat by the bamboo tube copying names one by one into the contest register. It was an old ledger with blue cloth covers, its corners worn to rags; the first few dozen pages recorded past contests, a page a year, and the top line of each the year's first place. At Zhou Heng's table Xiaoman saw the register lying open near the front, the ink going from new to old, old till it was yellow as autumn leaves. On one page the first-place name had been struck through with one straight stroke, the ink of the stroke newer than the name's; the name beneath had blurred in a water stain, past reading.

"Brother Zhou, why is this one struck out?" Zhou Heng didn't look up: "The struck-out ones are the ones no longer at the temple." "Dead?" "No longer at the temple. The books record whether you're here, not why. Why isn't mine to see to." He held out a hand. "Your slip." Xiaoman put his hand in the tube. The steward read out: "Shen Xiaoman — against Sun Ergou." Someone below laughed out loud.

exits.means: steps up onto the contest platform for the first round
